comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
REBAR-DEBUG PHASE 1 — mechanism confirmed; design-gated, no repair applied

Confirmed mechanism: an accepted forced-review request has no durable identity. `/rerun` resets its retry budget, places the sole `_rebar_force` event on the process-local asyncio queue, and returns 202. Accepted `recheck-review` likewise resets the budget, posts an affirmative queued reply, and only then returns a forced event that the worker requeues. The SQLite store contains only `voted` and `review_attempts`; after process loss, `reconcile_once` sees only an ordinary patchset event and skips it when Gerrit already has a vote.

Runtime proof: a real `/rerun` request returned 202 with `{queued:true,force:true}` and queue depth 1; after simulated restart the fresh queue was empty, the durable tables had no pending-force row, and real reconciliation of the same already-voted revision scanned 1/reviewed 0. Controls passed: a vote-less revision is reviewed by reconciliation, and direct `review_and_vote(force=True)` bypasses both vote guards and re-votes while force=False skips. Routine graceful shutdown may drain fast work; the proven loss window is hard death or the bounded drain/cancel window expiring.

Classification under the original-intent guard: `cannot-determine` / design decision required. ADR 0009 §7a, the runbook, and review policy promise an operator/contributor escape hatch that enqueues and re-reviews a stuck vote, which supports durability. But the original S4b story and ADR explicitly define the durable reconciler only for vote-less patchsets, the contributor story requires reset+enqueue+reply without persistence, and the introducing design chose an in-memory queue. No original epic explicitly requires an accepted forced request to survive restart. Adding `forced_pending` therefore creates retry/coalescing semantics rather than restoring an unambiguous documented contract.

Decision needed before Phase 2: should accepted `/rerun` and `recheck-review` requests be at-least-once durable across process loss? If yes, the design must define request generations/coalescing (avoiding an ABA clear), persist before budget reset/public acknowledgement, define stale requests after new revisions/closure, and clear only the matching successful forced review. No code changed.

comments.body: Plan-review remediation evidence (read-only production probe, 2026-08-09): queried Gerrit events-log with the checkout credential and inspected only event structure/approval transitions. Found 551 LLM-Review approval events: all were `comment-added`, and all carried both `patchSet.revision` and `patchSet.ref`. Shapes included 430 value-0 events, 114 0→+1 events, 4 0→-1 events, 2 initial +1 events, 1 initial -1 event, and 1 -1→+1 event. This proves a review-label/comment write emits the fresh patchset-bearing event needed to re-admit an old rerun target after the persisted cursor. No ticket/change content or credentials were logged. The revised plan also verifies the post-reset no-nonzero-vote state before acknowledging, so an admin/concurrent vote cannot create a falsely durable acceptance.

REBAR-DEBUG PHASE 2 — frozen test-contract card

```yaml
authoritative_contract: "Approved ticket plan + production Gerrit events-log probe recorded on this ticket: acceptance resets the exact revision to neutral 0 before acknowledgement; the resulting patchset-bearing comment-added event is the durable review-owed marker after process loss."
trigger_preconditions: "The exact revision has a nonzero Gerrit vote, a matching local voted row, an exhausted attempt budget, and its original patchset event is older than an already-persisted reconcile cursor. /rerun returns accepted and the old process queue contains the forced event; a replacement queue starts empty."
production_path: "Real FastAPI /rerun handler -> real DedupStore -> stateful production-shaped Gerrit fake at the external REST/events-log boundary -> real reconcile_once -> real review_and_vote."
test_tier: "Stateful component/integration test. A pure route, SQL, or reconciler unit test one tier lower cannot cross the queue-loss + Gerrit event + cursor + stale-dedup + voter seam that caused the defect."
observable_postcondition: "After discarding the accepted request’s old queue, one reconcile pass consumes the reset-emitted event and casts exactly one new vote for the same change/revision."
ci_gate: "pytest exact node; then make test."
negative_control: "Existing contrast coverage remains: a revision with any nonzero Gerrit vote is skipped, and a second pass after the recovered vote is idempotent."
collateral_invariants: "An unrelated voted row remains; the exact revision is recorded voted after the new successful vote; no other change is reviewed."
recovery: "A replacement process queue is empty; reconciliation alone completes the owed review from durable Gerrit + SQLite state."
fault_injection: "Process loss is injected at the proven seam immediately after HTTP acceptance and before dequeue by discarding the old asyncio queue; the external boundary is a stateful fake whose reset appends the production-observed comment-added shape after the persisted cursor."
```

The final RED oracle will be held out from the fixer. Collection/execution proof, GREEN, defect-seeded mutation, broader gates, and the original restart reproduction will be recorded after the repair.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
REBAR-DEBUG PHASE 2 — repair and proof complete

Root cause: accepted `/rerun` and `recheck-review` requests existed only as `_rebar_force` events in the process-local queue. After process loss, Gerrit still carried the old nonzero vote and SQLite still carried the matching `voted` row, so reconciliation skipped the revision before it could recreate the review.

Repair: both acceptance paths now reset the exact current revision to fixed neutral `LLM-Review: 0`, verify all accounts retain no nonzero vote, best-effort reset the retry budget, then enqueue/return the forced live event. The reset-emitted Gerrit `comment-added` event is the durable marker. Reconciliation queries Gerrit before local dedup; a definitive no-vote read clears only the exact stale row, while a Gerrit read error preserves dedup and holds the cursor back. Contributor text cannot select a label value or mint PASS/BLOCK; replies remain label-free. Public policy, ADR, deployment, and operator-runbook documentation now state this contract.

Held-out proof: `test_accepted_rerun_survives_restart_via_gerrit_reconcile` begins with an old nonzero Gerrit vote, matching stale SQLite dedup, an unrelated dedup row, an exhausted retry budget, and a cursor past the original patchset event. `/rerun` returns 202 and queues once; the old queue is discarded; a replacement queue is empty. One reconcile pass consumes the reset-emitted event and returns `{scanned: 1, reviewed: 1}`, casts exactly one new vote for the exact revision, and preserves the unrelated row.

Mutation proof: temporarily restoring the defective local-dedup-first branch made that held-out test fail with `{reviewed: 0}`; restoring Gerrit-first ordering returned it to GREEN.

Verification on current `origin/main`: plan review PASS/certified; focused review-bot/security suite 157 passed; newly-landed base tests 13 passed; `make lint` passed; `make typecheck` passed (491 files); `git diff --check` passed. Clean full CI-extra suite before the final two non-overlapping origin/main commits: 11,732 passed, 19 skipped, 255 deselected in 44m33s with `REBAR_REQUIRE_EXTRAS=1`. The first full run exposed a missing local `ui` extra (15 audit-page failures due solely to absent jinja2); installing the documented `dev + reviewbot + ui + metrics` extras made that cluster 15/15 green and the subsequent clean full run green.

Manual five-axis review found no blocking correctness, security, performance, maintainability, or test issue. One failure-atomicity correction was applied during review: once Gerrit neutral state is durable, a local `reset_attempts` failure is warned but does not falsely reject an already-accepted request.

(2) `/rerun` reset+verify latency/new fail-closed statuses are the approved durability-vs-availability contract; acknowledging before them would recreate the bug. compiled_state.description:
## Context

Accepted `/rerun` and `recheck-review` requests are currently represented only by a forced event in the process-local asyncio queue. If the receiver exits before that event is processed, the request disappears. Local dedup and the existing Gerrit `LLM-Review` vote then cause reconciliation to skip the revision.

The approved contract uses Gerrit as the durable source of truth: an accepted request first changes the exact revision to no nonzero `LLM-Review` vote. That label write also emits a fresh Gerrit `comment-added` event carrying the revision and ref, re-admitting even an old change to the reconciler’s events-log window. No `forced_pending` table is introduced.

## Proven root cause and capability evidence

Both acceptance paths currently reset the attempt budget and enqueue/return a forced event without first creating durable state. Reconciliation checks local `voted` state before Gerrit and therefore skips a revision whose stale local row survives after its Gerrit vote is reset. `review_and_vote` has the same local-first guard.

A read-only probe of the production Gerrit events-log on 2026-08-09 found 551 `LLM-Review` approval events. Every one was a `comment-added` event with both `patchSet.revision` and `patchSet.ref`; observed values included `0`, `-1`, and `1`. This verifies that a review-label write produces the fresh patchset-bearing event the reconciler consumes, independently of the original patchset-created event’s age.

## Security invariant update

The existing recheck documentation says the path never writes any label because its reply uses label-free `post_comment`. The approved vote-reset-first design intentionally narrows that invariant: an untrusted contributor comment can never choose a label value or mint a PASS/BLOCK. Only after privileged-side eligibility succeeds may the bot invoke a distinct reset operation whose fixed value is exactly neutral `0`. The affirmative/refusal reply still uses `post_comment` and remains provably label-free. Ineligible comments, malformed events, and failed eligibility checks write no label. Update the retrigger module documentation and tests to state this fixed-neutral-reset invariant; retain the existing `post_comment` body assertion unchanged.

## Plan

1. Add `GerritClient.reset_llm_review_vote(change_id, revision)`, which writes exactly `LLM-Review: 0` plus a rerun-request message on the exact revision.
2. After reset succeeds, call the existing all-accounts vote reader and require no nonzero `LLM-Review` vote. A surviving concurrent/admin vote is intentionally fail-closed: reject because the bot can reset only its own account’s vote and therefore cannot establish the durable marker.
3. On reset/write/read rejection, emit a warning keyed by change and revision. Return a non-success response for `/rerun`; for recheck, emit `RETRIGGER_REFUSED` and do not post the affirmative accepted reply.
4. For accepted `/rerun` and recheck, perform reset, verify, reset the retry-attempt budget, then enqueue/return the forced event.
5. Add `DedupStore.clear_voted(change_id, revision)`, implemented as an exact-key `DELETE FROM voted WHERE change_id=? AND revision=?`; it is distinct from `reset_attempts`, which deletes from `review_attempts`.
6. Reconcile only the bounded candidate set in the existing events-log window. Query Gerrit before trusting local dedup. A successful no-nonzero-vote result calls `clear_voted` and invokes the ordinary voter. The existing Gerrit-error branch preserves dedup, emits `reconcile_check_error`, and holds the cursor back for retry.
7. Preserve the normal skip when Gerrit has any nonzero vote. Preserve the forced live path for the accepted request already in memory.
8. Prove the complete restart path with a stateful Gerrit fake: reset appends a production-shaped `comment-added` event after an advanced cursor; a replacement queue starts empty; reconciliation consumes the event, clears matching stale dedup, and reviews the exact revision.
9. Run focused review-bot tests and repository gates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit/API test proves `/rerun` resets the exact revision before resetting attempts.
- [ ] Unit/API test proves `/rerun` returns HTTP 202 only after reset succeeds.
- [ ] Unit/API test proves `/rerun` returns HTTP 202 only after the verification read finds no nonzero vote.
- [ ] Unit/API failure test proves reset failure returns non-success and enqueues nothing.
- [ ] Unit/API failure test proves verification-read failure returns non-success and leaves attempts unchanged.
- [ ] Unit/API failure test proves a surviving nonzero vote returns non-success and emits a warning keyed by change/revision.
- [ ] Unit/retrigger test proves eligibility is decided before the fixed-neutral reset.
- [ ] Unit/retrigger test proves accepted recheck resets and verifies before resetting attempts.
- [ ] Unit/retrigger test proves the reset body fixes the label value at exactly `0`; contributor text cannot influence it.
- [ ] Unit/retrigger failure test proves an ineligible request writes no label.
- [ ] Unit/retrigger failure test proves reset/read/nonzero rejection produces no forced event and emits `RETRIGGER_REFUSED`.
- [ ] Existing unit test continues proving `post_comment` replies contain no `labels` member.
- [ ] Stateful reconciliation test proves reset appends a patchset-bearing `comment-added` event newer than an advanced cursor.
- [ ] Stateful restart test proves an empty replacement queue plus retained stale dedup is recovered from that event.
- [ ] Stateful invariant test proves `clear_voted` deletes only the matching row.
- [ ] Contrast test proves reconciliation skips a revision with any nonzero Gerrit vote.
- [ ] Error-path test proves a Gerrit vote-read failure preserves dedup and emits `reconcile_check_error`.
- [ ] Mutation proof restores local-dedup-first ordering and makes the held-out restart regression fail.
- [ ] Focused review-bot tests pass.
- [ ] `make lint` passes.
- [ ] `make typecheck` passes.
- [ ] `make test` passes.
